slides.title: Why is your *report so slow*
slides.voiceover: Is your report slow? Here's the likely reason.
slides.spoken: Is your report slow? Here's the likely reason.

slides.heading: *Slow* vs *fast*
slides.left:
LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls).
  SELECT SINGLE name1 FROM kna1
    WHERE kunnr = @ls-kunnr
    INTO @DATA(lv_name).
ENDLOOP.
slides.right:
SELECT kunnr, name1 FROM kna1
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
  WHERE kunnr = @lt_orders-kunnr
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_kna1).
slides.voiceover: A SELECT inside a loop means one database call for every row. Read the data once, then look it up in memory.
slides.spoken: A SELECT inside a loop means one database call for every row. Read the data once, then look it up in memory.

slides.title: Result
slides.detail: Then read lt_kna1 inside the loop.
slides.voiceover: Ten thousand calls become just one. Save this.
slides.spoken: Ten thousand calls become just one. Save this.

posts.caption:
Is your report taking 20 minutes instead of 2?

In most cases the cause is the same: a SELECT inside a LOOP. Every iteration is a separate trip to the database.

The fix: read the data once before the loop (JOIN or FOR ALL ENTRIES), then look it up in an internal table inside the loop. For large volumes, use a SORTED or HASHED table.
